failures.text: How does an idea get from a draft all the way to paper trading with real allocated capital?
failures.answer: Sir, an idea climbs a fixed staircase, and no step is skipped. A finding becomes a draft only when a fixed count how often it fires. It is registered once you say yes, then tested on 2000-2023 at a the strict pass mark and run as a paper book on live sessions (20 recorded). It is admitted only after it beats random picks and the average stock on 10 separate sessions after costs and passes a check that no future data leaked in, and then you say yes again; the final real-money gate comes after that. Right now no rule has reached the admitted step: the stock rules are at the paper-trial step (breakouts 8 of 20 sessions, pullbacks 7, reversals 9) and the options line at 6 of 20.

problems.why: It opens with the internal term "staircase", and the garbled phrases "a fixed count how often it fires" and "at a the strict pass mark" are hard for a beginner to follow.

results.text: What exactly is your job for me? One paragraph.
results.answer: Sir, my job is to be your assistant for the Indian market, on paper only. Each evening I re-rate every holding in your account and write a cut list, and I keep paper books that test ideas by rules, including one that acts on that list. Each morning I give you the market view and the day's plan, and I answer your questions from my own data and tests, saying plainly when a number is missing or an idea is untested. I cannot place or change any real trade, and only you can approve research drafts or change anything.

results.text: If RSI is 28 on the Nifty daily, what does that tell you, and what would you do?
results.answer: Sir, RSI is a 0-100 gauge of recent buying against selling, and 28 on the Nifty daily means oversold: the index has fallen hard and fast. Ananta tested RSI under 30 on stocks, not on the Nifty itself, and trades bought that way earned more over the next 20 sessions (about +2.5% in 2000-2017 and +1.9% in 2018-2023), so it is a mild point in favour of a bounce. As a trade, I would not buy only because of the reading: stay small and staggered, and I'd reverse that if the Nifty keeps closing lower with RSI still under 30, because oversold can stay oversold. For comparison, the Nifty's RSI at the last close (2 Nov) was 61, so we are nowhere near that zone now.

results.text: What is the one risk rule that stops a bad day from becoming a bad month?
results.answer: Sir, it is the daily loss limit: at a 5% loss for the day, every position is closed and no new entry is made until the next session. That caps one bad day, so it cannot snowball into a bad week or month. Two limits sit behind it: the rule that pauses trading after a 22% fall below the peak stops new buys until you resume, and the rule only acts during market hours, so an overnight gap can still go past 5%.

results.text: The twin is six sessions in and the managed book is on session one of sixty. Why two different clocks on the same holdings?
results.answer: Sir, the twin is on 7 of 60 sessions, not six. They are two different experiments, so each has its own clock that starts when its own rules begin. The twin started on 23 Oct and only moves money between stocks, options and cash to keep the split. The managed book began later, with its first paper buys on 2 Nov: it acts on the cut list and buys a replacement for each cut. Both are judged after 60 sessions against the frozen original and the Nifty 500, and nothing is read into either before then.

results.text: Give me a daily checklist, five lines, for reading your morning view.
results.answer: Sir, five lines, in this order: 1) Check the headline: where the Nifty closed and whether it is above or below its 50- and 200-day averages. 2) Read the lines that decide the day: above 23,511 was an up day and below 23,370 a down day on the last view; take the new ones from the day's view. 3) Read "Our chances, honestly": the rule forecast and the daily call each with their record against a coin flip, and trust none that is below it. 4) Look at the Watch list: expiry days, results, the F&O ban list and the guardrails. 5) Last, see what Ananta is doing: the practice buys, the options line's decision and your holdings' notes, remembering the practice buys are paper, not your money.
